title: Can the rope be perfectly flat?
hook: Raise the ends of a rope while a weight hangs from its middle.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: The two upward components must add to 200 N. At 30° each side needs 200 N; at 10° the vertical fraction is smaller, so each side needs about 576 N.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: The two upward components must add to 200 N. At 30° each side needs 200 N; at 10° the vertical fraction is smaller, so each side needs about 576 N.

claims.text: The two upward components must add to 200 N. At 30° each side needs 200 N; at 10° the vertical fraction is smaller, so each side needs about 576 N. Static, symmetric, ideal massless rope. Perfectly horizontal rope cannot supply an upward component in this model.
claims.source: Vertical equilibrium: 2 T sin(theta) = 200 N. T(30°)=200 N; T(10°)=575.877 N.

recall.question: Two identical ropes hold a 100 N weight. Each makes 30° with the horizontal. What is the tension in each?
recall.why: Each tension contributes half its value upward: 2 × T × 0.5 = 100 N.
